So we need to edit a systemd unit file to enable it (likely set enabled=true or ensure it's started). In Rocky Linux/RHEL, services are managed by systemd. To enable a service, we can use systemctl enable pcscd.service. But the remediation script likely wants to modify the unit file to have [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target etc. Or ensure the service is enabled via a drop-in or the unit file itself.

But the question: "You are the Remedy agent remediating ONE OpenSCAP finding on Rocky Linux 10. You MUST use ONLY the provided tools: run_cmd, read_file, write_file. Rules: ... Which file to modify to enable the pcscd service?" So we need to read the unit file, maybe edit it to set enabled.

Thus answer: The file is /usr/lib/systemd/system/pcscd.service (or /etc/systemd/system/pcscd.service). In RHEL, the unit files are in /usr/lib/systemd/system/ and overrides can be in /etc/systemd/system/. To enable, we can create an override in /etc/systemd/system/pcscd.service.d/ or just edit the unit.

Given typical OpenSCAP remediation for enabling a service: they often edit the unit file to set "Enabled=true" in the [Install] section or add a WantedBy. So the file to modify is /usr/lib/systemd/system/pcscd.service.

Thus answer: /usr/lib/systemd/system/pcscd.service.
